faq.q: What is a solar AMC?
faq.a: A solar AMC is an annual maintenance contract: an agreement for scheduled visits, inspections and a stated way of handling faults, usually for twelve months at a time.

faq.q: Does a solar AMC cover spare parts?
faq.a: It depends on the contract. Some AMCs cover visits and labour only, with parts quoted separately; others include certain parts. Ask for this in writing before signing any AMC.

faq.q: How often are visits done?
faq.a: It depends on the plan and the site. Dusty locations and larger plants usually need more frequent visits. We agree the schedule with you and write it into the contract.

faq.q: Is an AMC the same as my panel warranty?
faq.a: No. A warranty is the manufacturer's promise about product defects or performance. An AMC is a service arrangement for upkeep. They work together; see our guide to solar panel warranties.

faq.q: Can you take over maintenance of a system someone else installed?
faq.a: Usually yes. We start with an inspection so the contract reflects the system's actual condition. Tell us the make and size and we will confirm.

faq.q: How early should I renew my solar AMC?
faq.a: A few weeks before the end date is sensible, so any changes to scope can be agreed and the new period starts the day the old one ends.

faq.q: Can I change the plan when I renew?
faq.a: Yes. Renewal is the right moment to change visit frequency, add or remove cleaning, or add remote monitoring.

faq.q: My AMC was with another company. Can I renew with you?
faq.a: You can start a new contract with us. We usually begin with an inspection so the scope reflects the system as it is now.

faq.q: What if my AMC already expired?
faq.a: Send a request anyway. We will suggest an inspection first and then a contract that reflects what we find.

faq.q: Does solar need maintenance at all?
faq.a: Solar has no major moving parts, but it still needs periodic cleaning and inspection. Neglected systems commonly lose output slowly and nobody notices.

faq.q: How much does maintenance cost?
faq.a: It depends on system size, site access and how often visits are needed. We quote after understanding your system and list exactly what is included.

faq.q: Do I need an AMC or can I book single visits?
faq.a: Both work. A single visit suits a one-off check; an AMC suits owners who want scheduled visits and a record over time.

faq.q: Can you maintain any inverter brand?
faq.a: Tell us the make and model when you enquire and we will confirm what we can service.

faq.q: Do solar panels really need cleaning?
faq.a: In most locations, yes. Rain removes some dust but not all, and droppings or film can stay for months. Clean panels let more light through.

faq.q: How do I know whether cleaning would help?
faq.a: Compare generation on similar sunny days before and after cleaning. A clear jump tells you soiling was costing you output.

faq.q: Can I clean panels myself?
faq.a: Light dust from ground level can be hosed with water at low pressure. Roof access carries a fall risk, so for rooftops we recommend people trained to work at height.

faq.q: Is panel cleaning included in an AMC?
faq.a: That depends on the plan. We state clearly in the contract whether cleaning is included, extra, or on request.

faq.q: Why does my solar inverter keep tripping?
faq.a: Common causes are grid voltage out of range, overheating, an earth fault or a loose connection. The error log and on-site measurements show which.

faq.q: Should I open the inverter to check?
faq.a: No. Inverters carry dangerous DC and AC voltages. Photograph the display and call a qualified technician.

faq.q: Which inverter brands do you service?
faq.a: Tell us the make and model and we will confirm whether we can service it.

faq.q: Will repair affect my warranty?
faq.a: It can. If your inverter is under warranty, contact the manufacturer or installer first, or tell us and we will help work out the right route.

faq.q: What does a service visit cost?

faq.q: What is solar O&M?
faq.a: O&M stands for operations and maintenance: the routine upkeep, monitoring and fault handling that keeps a solar plant producing as designed.

faq.q: Can you take over O&M from the original installer?
faq.a: Often yes. We start with an assessment and review of the plant's history so the new scope reflects its real condition.

faq.q: Do you work with plants of any size?
faq.a: Tell us your capacity and site type and we will confirm whether we can take it on.

faq.q: Does my inverter already have monitoring?
faq.a: Many modern inverters include a Wi-Fi or app-based monitoring feature. Tell us the make and model and we can check what yours supports.

faq.q: Do I need monitoring if I have an AMC?
faq.a: It is not required, but it helps. Monitoring can show problems between visits.

faq.q: Will monitoring tell me when panels need cleaning?
faq.a: It can show a generation decline that suggests soiling, but only a visit confirms the cause.

faq.q: How big a system do I need?
faq.a: It depends on your electricity usage, available roof space and budget. A survey and your recent bills let us size it.

faq.q: Do I get a subsidy?
faq.a: Eligibility depends on the scheme and your category. See the official PM Surya Ghar portal for current rules.

faq.q: How long does installation take?
faq.a: It depends on approvals, the site and equipment. We give an expected schedule with the proposal.

faq.q: Will the system need maintenance?
faq.a: Yes, light but regular: cleaning and periodic inspection. An AMC is one way to arrange it.
